5.01.t: Vertebra in Hand — Which Region, Which Level
5.01.b:
### Parts of a typical vertebra
- **Body** in front → **pedicles** → **laminae** meet behind → **spinous process**; ring = **spinal canal**
  [[FIG: Fig 5.1 · 5.01
- **Transverse process** → between pedicle and lamina · 4 **articular processes** → 2 superior + 2 inferior = **facet joints** (Handbook)
- **Pars interarticularis** → strut between the articular processes, best seen on a **coronal** cut · **foramen** → between two pedicles, root exits (Handbook)
- Count → **33** = 7 cervical · 12 thoracic · 5 lumbar · 5 sacral (fused) · 4 coccygeal (Handbook)

### Which region? — one look
| Feature | Cervical | Thoracic | Lumbar |
|---|---|---|---|
| Body | Small, oval, **uncinate process** (uncus) | **Heart-shaped**, costal facets | Big, **kidney-shaped** |
| Transverse process | **Foramen transversarium** | **Costal facet** for the rib tubercle | Long, thin, no facet |
| Spinous process | Short, **bifid** (C3–C6) | Long, points **down** | Short, square, **hatchet** |
| Canal | Big, triangular | Small, round | Triangular |
| Facet plane | ≈45° → all movements | **Coronal** → rotation | **Sagittal** → flexion–extension |

(Handbook; Netter)
[[FIG: Fig 5.2, 5.3, 5.4, 5.5 · 5.01

- Hold it → hole in the transverse process = **cervical** · rib facet on the body = **thoracic** · neither = **lumbar**

|---|---|---|

| **T10** | One rib only | **Single** facet for rib 10 |

5.02.b:
### Hold C1 and C2 → point & say
| Point to | C1 (atlas) | C2 (axis) |
|---|---|---|
| Front | **Anterior arch** + facet for the dens | **Dens** (odontoid) |
| Side | **Lateral masses** → up to the condyles, down to C2 | Superior facets → C1; **pars** → hangman's fracture |
| Back | Posterior arch + **groove for the vertebral artery** (upper surface) | Big **bifid spine** → landmark on X-ray |
| What it lacks | **No body**, no spinous process | — |

(Handbook; Netter)
[[FIG: Fig 5.12, 5.13, 5.14 · 5.02

- **Dens = the embryonic body of C1**, fused to C2 → see 5.09 (Handbook)
- O–C1 → nodding ("yes") · C1–C2 → rotation ("no"), a **pivot synovial** joint (Handbook)

CLINICAL PEARL — odontoid type 2
- Waist of the dens = **watershed** between head and base → poorest blood supply (Handbook)
- So **type 2** = commonest odontoid fracture **and** highest nonunion (Handbook)

### Ligaments of the craniocervical junction
| Ligament | Runs | Job |
|---|---|---|
| **Transverse** | Lateral mass → lateral mass, behind the dens | Holds the dens → **main C1–C2 stabiliser** |
| **Cruciate** | Transverse + vertical bands | Same, with up/down bands |
| **Alar** | Sides of the dens → occipital condyles | Limit rotation · avulsion = **type 3 condyle fracture** |
| **Apical** | Dens tip → foramen magnum | Weak, minor |
| **Tectorial membrane** | Covers them → continues down as the **PLL (posterior longitudinal ligament)** | Limits flexion |

(Handbook; Netter)
[[FIG: Fig 5.15, 5.16 · 5.02

- Mnemonic → "**T**ransverse **T**akes the load, **A**lar **A**nchors rotation, **T**ectorial **T**urns into the PLL"

CLINICAL PEARL — craniocervical junction
- **Occipital condyle fracture** → most often injured nerve = **hypoglossal (CN XII)** (Handbook)
- **Grisel's syndrome** → C1–C2 rotatory subluxation in a **child after a throat infection** → urgent assessment (Handbook)
- **Down syndrome, rheumatoid arthritis** → lax or eroded **transverse ligament** → atlantoaxial instability (Handbook)

### Numbers on the C1–C2 X-ray
- **ADI** (atlantodental interval) → normal **≤3 mm** · >5 mm → transverse torn · >7.5 mm → alar + apical too (Handbook)
  [[FIG: Fig 5.17, 5.18 · 5.02
- **PADI** (posterior ADI = space for the cord) → normal 18–19 mm · **<14 mm → surgery**; better predictor of neurology than ADI (Handbook)
- **Rule of Spence** → lateral masses overhang C2 by **>7 mm** (both sides added) → transverse ligament torn (Handbook)

PITFALL — ADI in children
- Handbook gives adult values (≤3 mm); children have more cartilage and lax ligaments
- Say → "**3 mm in adults, up to 5 mm in children**"

5.03.b:
### Uncovertebral joint (Luschka)
- **Uncus** of the body below → meets the body above · **cervical only** (C3–C7) · a "**pseudo-joint**" that blocks lateral slide (Handbook)
  [[FIG: Fig 5.19 · 5.03
- Osteophytes here → narrow the **foramen** from in front → radiculopathy
- **Vertebral artery lies just lateral** → the uncus is the **lateral limit** of anterior decompression

### Vertebral artery — the four parts
| Part | Course | Point to |
|---|---|---|
| **V1** pre-foraminal | Subclavian → up in front of C7 transverse process | Enters the **C6** foramen |
| **V2** foraminal | Through the foramina **C6 → C1** | Lateral to the uncus |
| **V3** extradural | Out of C1 foramen → **behind the lateral mass** → groove on the C1 posterior arch | Suboccipital triangle |
| **V4** intradural | Pierces the dura → joins the other one | **Basilar** artery at the pons |

(Netter)
[[FIG: Fig 5.20, 5.21 · 5.03

- Enters **C6** in ≈93%; the rest enter C5, C4 or C7, often with an odd origin (Uchino 2013)
- **C7** foramen → usually veins only → the artery runs **in front of** C7, not through it (Netter)

MUST-KNOW — 60-second answer: "course of the vertebral artery in the cervical spine"
- **First branch of the subclavian** → passes in front of C7 → enters the **C6 foramen transversarium** (≈93%)
- **V2** → climbs through the foramina C6 → C1, **lateral to the uncinate processes**
- **V3** → leaves C1, curves **behind the C1 lateral mass**, lies in the **groove on top of the posterior arch** → suboccipital triangle
- **V4** → pierces the posterior atlanto-occipital membrane + dura → foramen magnum → joins the other → **basilar**
- At risk → anterior decompression too lateral · C1 posterior dissection too lateral · C1–C2 screws

### Lateral mass vs pedicle
- Subaxial → **lateral mass** = the square block between superior and inferior facets → standard screw site (Kim)
  [[FIG: Fig 5.22, 5.23 · 5.03
- **Pedicle** → small, close to the artery (lateral) and root (below) → used mostly at **C2 and C7** (Kim)
- C2 → **pars** screw vs **pedicle** screw → both run near the artery; check the CT first (Kim)

5.04.b:
### Thoracic vertebrae
- **Rib head** → demifacets on two bodies + disc · **tubercle** → facet on the transverse process (Netter)
  [[FIG: Fig 5.24, 5.25, 5.26, 5.27 · 5.04
- Ribs + sternum → the stiffest part of the spine → fractures need big force
- Pedicles → **narrowest T4 ≈4.5 mm**, tilted in ≈14° → widest T12 ≈7.8 mm, almost straight (Vaccaro 1995)

### Lumbar vertebrae
- **Pars** → the weak neck between the facets → **spondylolysis**, commonest at **L5** (Handbook)
  [[FIG: Fig 5.28, 5.29, 5.30 · 5.04
- Extras → **mamillary process** (on the superior facet) + **accessory process** (root of the transverse process) (Netter)
- Pedicle entry → **transverse process** line meets the **lateral edge of the superior facet** (mamillary process) (Netter)
- Facets → **sagittal** → resist rotation · **L5–S1** turns coronal → resists forward slip

### Sacrum & coccyx
- 5 fused vertebrae → **promontory** (front of S1), **ala** (wings), 4 pairs of foramina, **sacral hiatus** (S4–S5) (Netter)
  [[FIG: Fig 5.31, 5.32 · 5.04
- **Auricular surface** → SI (sacroiliac) joint · sacrum = **keystone** of the pelvic ring (Handbook)
- **L5 root** runs over the **ala** → at risk in sacral fractures and iliosacral screws (Handbook)
- **S1** → biggest body + widest corridor → standard iliosacral screw target

5.05.t: Joints, Disc & Ligaments of the Spine
5.05.b:
### Intervertebral disc
| Part | Made of | Job |
|---|---|---|
| **Annulus fibrosus** | **Type I** collagen | Resists **tension**, holds the nucleus |
| **Nucleus pulposus** | **Type II** collagen + proteoglycans, water | Resists **compression** |

(Handbook)
[[FIG: Fig 5.33, 5.34 · 5.05

- Discs → **¼ of spinal height**; first disc = **C2–C3**, last = L5–S1 (Handbook)
- **Curves** come from **disc** shape (front taller than back), not vertebral body height (Handbook)
- Adult disc → **no vessels** → fed by diffusion through the endplates → poor healing

### Facet joints
- **Synovial** joints → from **C0–C1 to L5–S1** (Handbook)
  [[FIG: Fig 5.35, 5.36 · 5.05
- **Plane decides motion** → cervical 45° · thoracic coronal · lumbar sagittal (table in 5.01)
- Arthritic facet + thick ligamentum flavum → **lateral recess** stenosis

### Ligaments and Denis's three columns
| Ligament | Where | Note |
|---|---|---|
| **ALL** (anterior longitudinal) | Front of bodies, wide | Strong · torn in extension |
| **PLL** (posterior longitudinal) | Back of bodies, **inside the canal** | Narrow at the sides → **posterolateral** disc herniation |
| **Ligamentum flavum** | Lamina → lamina | Yellow (elastin) · thickens in stenosis |
| **Interspinous / supraspinous** | Between / over the spines | Part of the **PLC** (posterior ligamentous complex) |
| **Intertransverse** | Transverse → transverse | Minor |

(Handbook; Netter)
[[FIG: Fig 5.37, 5.38 · 5.05

| Column | Contains | Fracture that breaks it |
|---|---|---|
| **Anterior** | ALL + front ⅔ of body and disc | Compression → anterior only |
| **Middle** | Back ⅓ of body and disc + **PLL** | **Burst** → anterior + middle |
| **Posterior** | Arch + **PLC** | Flexion–distraction (**Chance**) → posterior first; fracture–dislocation → all 3 |

(Handbook)

- Rule → **middle column broken = unstable** (Denis) → the bone in the middle column can enter the canal

- **Ankylosing spondylitis, DISH (diffuse idiopathic skeletal hyperostosis), old fusion** → long rigid lever → **chalk-stick** fracture after minor trauma (Handbook)
- Clinical clearance not enough → **CT is mandatory** even if painless and neurologically normal (Handbook)

5.06.b:
### Canal zones
| Zone | Where | Walls |
|---|---|---|
| **Central canal** | Dural sac → cord + intradural roots | Front → body, disc, PLL · back → lamina, ligamentum flavum |
| **Zone 1 — lateral recess** | Dura → foramen | Back → **superior articular process** · front → disc **without PLL** |
| **Zone 2 — foramen** | The foramen itself | Pedicle above and below |
| **Zone 3 — extraforaminal** | Outside the foramen | No bony walls |

(Handbook)
[[FIG: Fig 5.39, 5.40 · 5.06

### Cord, conus and roots
- Cord ends at **L1–L2** in adults (mean lower third of L1; range T12 → L3) (Saifuddin 1998) · at **L3 at birth** (Orthobullets)
  [[FIG: Fig 5.41 · 5.06
- Dural sac → **S2** · filum terminale → coccyx (Netter)
- **31 segments** → 8 C, 12 T, 5 L, 5 S, 1 Co → 8 cervical nerves for 7 vertebrae (Handbook)
- Cord segment vs bone → cervical same level · T1–T6 +1 · T7–T10 +2 · lumbar segments opposite T11–T12 · sacral opposite L1 (Handbook)

### Root–level rules
- **Cervical** → root exits **above** its pedicle (C6 root at C5–C6) · **C8** exits below C7 (Handbook)
- From **T1 down** → root exits **below** its pedicle (Handbook)
  [[FIG: Fig 5.42, 5.43, 5.44 · 5.06
- Root leaves the dura **one level above** its foramen → long lumbar roots = **cauda equina** (Handbook)

| Disc | Paracentral (commonest) | Foraminal |
|---|---|---|
| **C6–C7** | **C7** root | **C7** root |
| **L4–L5** | **L5** root (traversing) | **L4** root (exiting) |

(Handbook)

- Mnemonic → **F**oraminal = **E**arly number · para**C**entral = **L**ate number (Handbook)

### Cord tracts → incomplete cord syndromes (anatomy only)
| Tract | Carries | Crosses |
|---|---|---|
| **Lateral spinothalamic** | Pain, temperature | At **entry level** in the cord |
| **Posterior columns** | Proprioception, vibration, fine touch | In the **medulla** |
| **Lateral corticospinal** | Voluntary motor (80%) | In the **medulla** |

(Handbook)
[[FIG: Fig 5.45, 5.46 · 5.06

- Lamination → **arms medial, legs lateral** → central cord syndrome hits the **hands** most (Handbook)

| Syndrome | Mechanism | Lost | Kept |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Central cord** | Hyperextension, old spondylotic neck | Arms > legs, hands worst | Sacral sparing |
| **Anterior cord** | Hyperflexion | Motor + pain/temperature | **Posterior columns** · worst prognosis |
| **Brown-Séquard** | Hemisection | Same-side motor + position · opposite-side pain/temperature | Best prognosis |
| **Posterior cord** | Hyperextension (rare) | Deep sensation | Motor, pain |

(Handbook)

|---|---|---|

| **Neural crest** | **Dorsal root ganglia**, sympathetic chain, pia, peripheral nerves | — |

### Somites and resegmentation
1) **42–44 pairs** of somites beside the notochord → 4 occipital · **8 cervical** · 12 T · 5 L · 5 S · 8–10 Co (Campbell)
[[FIG: Fig 5.55 · 5.09
2) Each sclerotome **splits** → loose cranial half + dense caudal half (Kim)
3) **Resegmentation** → caudal half of one + cranial half of the next = **one vertebra** (Campbell)
4) The **disc** forms at the line between the two halves (Kim)

- Result → vertebra sits **between two somites** → nerve exits between vertebrae, segmental artery crosses mid-body
- **8 cervical somites → 7 vertebrae → 8 cervical nerves** (Campbell)
- Stages → **membranous** wk 3 → **cartilage** wk 4 → **bone** wk 7–8, from mid-thoracic (Kim) · **PAX1** fault → Klippel-Feil (Campbell)

### Failure of formation vs failure of segmentation
| Failure of … | Partial | Complete | Growth |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Formation** (half not built) | **Wedge** vertebra | **Hemivertebra** (butterfly = central cleft) | Extra growth on the hemi side → curve |
| **Segmentation** (not separated) | **Unilateral bar** | **Block** vertebra | Bar = tether on one side · block = least curve |

(Campbell; Handbook)

- Mnemonic → **F**ormation = **F**orgot half · **S**egmentation = **S**tuck together
- Critical time **weeks 5–6** · worst → **unilateral bar + opposite hemivertebra** → 6–7°/year · bar alone 5°/year · block → least (Campbell)
- **Klippel-Feil** = failure of **segmentation** of the cervical spine → short neck, low hairline, stiff neck; full triad in <50% (Handbook; Campbell)
- **Diastematomyelia** → a bony spicule splits the cord → commonest intraspinal anomaly in congenital scoliosis (Shen 2013; Campbell)

- Fusion **above C3** → **no contact sports** (Handbook)
- Surgery → instability or basilar invagination · neurological signs · **chalk-stick fracture** through the fused block (highly unstable) (Handbook)

| Test | Why it works (anatomy) | Trap |

| **Spurling** | Extension + side-bend + rotation + axial load → **narrows the foramen** on that side (Handbook) | Shoulder pain → no change |
| **Lhermitte** | Neck flexion stretches the **cord** → electric shock down the spine | Cord lesion (myelopathy, MS), not a root |
| **Hoffmann** | Flick the middle-finger nail → thumb flexes → **UMN** (upper motor neuron) sign | Present in some normal people |
| **SLR** (straight leg raise) | Hip flexion, knee straight → pulls **L5–S1** roots 30–70° (Handbook) | >70° → hamstrings, non-specific |
| **Crossed SLR** | Raising the good leg pulls the dura → pain in the bad leg (Handbook) | Strong sign → big disc |
| **Bowstring** | Knee bent at pain → press the **sciatic nerve** in the popliteal fossa (Handbook) | — |
| **Femoral stretch** | Prone, knee bent, hip extended → pulls **L2–L4** (Handbook) | Psoas or hip pain |
